note: Initial planning baseline; GitHub is canonical for ongoing issue status.

milestones.title: M0 — Feasibility and decisions
milestones.description: Prove native Codex approval behavior and event coverage; record runtime, process, trust, and licensing decisions before application scaffolding.

milestones.title: M1 — Local foundation
milestones.description: Deliver the selected runtime scaffold, connector-neutral contracts, SQLite audit persistence, authenticated local service, and persistent project/task UI.

milestones.title: M2 — Registered Codex sessions
milestones.description: Run durable registered root/child sessions with scoped context, MCP identity, event ingestion, and workspace isolation.

milestones.title: M3 — Human governance
milestones.description: Human decisions resolve only the exact native pending action; fail closed across errors and recovery; inspect activity, changes, context, and decision ancestry.

milestones.title: M4 — Conversation routing
milestones.description: Automatically route terminal child observations to parent inboxes and support bounded parent/human replies without granting authority through classification.

milestones.title: M5 — Personas, artifacts, GitHub
milestones.description: Deliver versioned personas/skills, logical artifact freshness and context protocols, and optional governed GitHub repository/issue workflows.

milestones.title: M6 — MVP release readiness
milestones.description: Demonstrate all eight PRD acceptance criteria against a supported native Codex version and ship documented local onboarding with security/recovery evidence.

milestones.title: M7 — Delegation and portability
milestones.description: Post-MVP: add bounded delegated authority, transparent recommendation bundles, and redacted portable project archives.

issues.title: Prove native Codex approval pause, accept, deny, and failure behavior
issues.outcome: Establish whether the central exact-action governance promise is enforceable through a supported Codex interface.
issues.scope: Evaluate an AGCP-owned app-server process in a disposable workspace. Record CLI version, generated schema, initialization, approval configuration, native request/response identity, payload completeness, and timeout/disconnect observations. Do not build the product UI or rely on simulated approvals as proof.
acceptance: A supported native command approval is received and its side effect is absent while the response is withheld; capture a bounded observation interval.
Separate accept and deny cases show that only the selected original pending command can execute; demonstrate two concurrent requests cannot be cross-resolved.
Inventory command, file-change, network/permission and MCP approval coverage, classifying each as proven, untested, or unavailable. Flag insufficient immutable action detail.
Record timeout, client/process disconnect and restart behavior, exact one-action native decisions, and a go/no-go conclusion with sanitized evidence.
issues.verification: Use harmless sentinel files in a scratch workspace; record before/pending/after state, native correlation identifiers, and CLI version. Keep raw sessions and credentials out of Git. If a model-backed run is unavailable, report the missing evidence and leave the issue open.

issues.title: Map session events and direct Codex UI coexistence limits
issues.outcome: Define what the session inspector and automatic parent routing can observe, including direct/native Codex interaction.
issues.scope: Create a capability matrix for AGCP-owned sessions: message deltas, final messages, tools/results, diffs, terminal turns, failures, interruptions, reconnect and history retrieval. Investigate supported shared/native UI interaction without desktop data scraping.
acceptance: Document event ordering, stable identifiers, duplicate delivery, replay/history coverage, and transcript gaps for the tested CLI version.
Demonstrate a terminal child question can be observed without a child MCP report.
Prove or explicitly mark unsupported simultaneous/direct native UI use; specify approval ownership and conflict behavior if it is supported.
Publish a connector/inspector capability matrix and recommended MVP boundary with sanitized evidence.
issues.verification: Capture synthetic turns and interruptions, compare the supported protocol history with received events, and document missing coverage. This is a research report, not a promise of desktop attachment support.

issues.title: Select runtime, trust boundaries, workspace strategy, and licensing direction
issues.outcome: Finish the architectural decisions needed to build a secure local application without speculative scaffolding.
issues.scope: Complete ADR 0002 using both spikes. Compare local web UI/service, Electron and Tauri; select runtime, package manager, SQLite/migrations, IPC, process ownership and initial OS support. Define threat model, key storage, retention and workspace strategy. Record license selection or an explicit owned deferral.
acceptance: ADR 0002 is accepted with alternatives, consequences, version choices, repository layout, and linked spike evidence.
Threat model covers UI/service authentication, origin/CSRF if relevant, MCP capability scope, same-user processes, host administrator limits, key loss, and logs.
Define exact action canonicalization/signature boundary, one-shot delivery and restart recovery; distinguish AGCP verification from Codex native response handling.
Record isolated workspace/worktree ownership, supported session mode, and licensing/distribution decision or a release-blocking follow-up.
issues.verification: Review all technical-spec open decisions. Every unresolved release-critical item has an owner and a blocking issue; the chosen architecture can support the proven native approval flow.

issues.title: Scaffold the chosen application workspace and runtime CI
issues.outcome: Make the accepted runtime architecture runnable and verifiable from a clean checkout.
issues.scope: Create actual application/service/domain/connector packages as selected in ADR 0002, a tracked lockfile, configuration example, and CI build/type/lint checks. Preserve the existing documentation check.
acceptance: Documented install, development and build commands work on the initial supported OS.
Package boundaries keep domain code independent of Codex-specific wire types and UI rendering.
CI runs the real build and focused automated checks using pinned runtime/dependency choices.
Application state, credentials and generated output stay outside tracked source; sample configuration contains placeholders only.
issues.verification: Run setup from a clean checkout or equivalent disposable environment, execute documented build/check commands, and confirm no local state appears in git status.

issues.title: Define neutral entities, events, and task/session state transitions
issues.outcome: Give each subsystem stable identifiers and explicit legal transitions before persistence and connector implementation.
issues.scope: Define project/task/session/persona/artifact/approval/decision/authority/message/observation/audit contracts. Separate task acceptance from session turn completion and define event schema versions and source provenance.
acceptance: Contracts cover the technical-spec entities with project scope, stable IDs and versioned events.
Legal state transitions are documented; invalid transitions and cross-project identifiers are rejected.
Task completed/accepted state is distinct from model turn completion and observation labels.
Codex wire payloads do not enter public domain contracts; unknown connector events have a defined handling path.
issues.verification: Use transition-table and serialization checks for invalid states, missing identity, duplicate source events, and cross-project boundaries.

issues.title: Implement SQLite migrations, durable graph state, and hash-linked audit events
issues.outcome: Persist canonical local governance records and their event history with explicit integrity limits.
issues.scope: Create migrations, transactions, event IDs, source-event idempotency and audit hash linkage. Keep raw content optional and separate from metadata; implement the integrity/checkpoint strategy chosen in M0.
acceptance: A fresh database and supported migration path reconstruct project/task state after restart.
State changes and corresponding audit writes commit atomically; duplicate source events do not duplicate effects.
Audit verification detects modified/missing/reordered stored events within the stated threat model.
Storage paths remain outside repositories, with documented permissions, retention boundaries and backup/recovery behavior.
issues.verification: Exercise migration, rollback on write failure, duplicate delivery, restart reconstruction and deliberate audit-chain corruption using synthetic fixtures.

issues.title: Build authenticated local project/task APIs and scoped identity
issues.outcome: Expose local project/task operations without trusting caller-supplied project or authority claims.
issues.scope: Implement the local service boundary selected in M0, project and task CRUD/lifecycle operations, authenticated UI access, session-capability issuance/revocation primitives and minimal diagnostics.
acceptance: The service is local-only by default and rejects unauthenticated requests.
Project/task reads and writes enforce scope and legal parentage, preventing cycles and cross-project references.
Capability credentials are scoped, short-lived and revocable; ordinary logs contain no secret material.
Apply origin/CSRF and filesystem/process access controls required by the selected transport.
issues.verification: Exercise invalid/revoked credentials, cross-project reads/writes, cyclic graphs, foreign parents and local service restart. Verify allowed operations still work.

issues.title: Create local project workspace UI and persistent task tree
issues.outcome: Let the operator create a local project and inspect objectives, task ownership and actionable state.
issues.scope: Build a basic project view, manual child task creation, state/status presentation and task detail/chat shell. Clearly show unavailable connector/chat capabilities before M2.
acceptance: A user creates a project and root task, adds valid child tasks, and sees the tree after app restart.
Task details expose objective, owner/persona references and actionable versus idle/failed states.
Empty, loading and error states explain the next available action without invented live status.
Keyboard navigation and focus work for project selection and task tree/detail interaction.
issues.verification: Run a UI flow covering creation, invalid child handling, navigation and restart persistence. Add focused interaction checks around the tree state.

issues.title: Implement owned Codex connector lifecycle and capability negotiation
issues.outcome: Start, resume, message, interrupt and terminate registered Codex sessions through the proven adapter.
issues.scope: Implement the supported versioned app-server adapter and session bindings from M0. Perform protocol initialization, capability detection, lifecycle mapping and process shutdown. Expose unknown/unsupported capabilities explicitly.
acceptance: A project task starts a root session and records its original native session binding.
Supported message/interrupt/resume/terminate operations map to valid domain transitions.
Disconnect, unsupported protocol/version and process failure are visible and never silently grant pending approvals.
Adapter tests use pinned sanitized protocol fixtures; a documented live smoke run verifies supported lifecycle behavior.
issues.verification: Exercise lifecycle and error paths with fixtures plus one native supported-version session. Do not claim native proof from mocked responses alone.

issues.title: Ingest session activity and replay it into a durable inspector timeline
issues.outcome: Provide reliable event evidence for approvals, conversation routing and session inspection.
issues.scope: Normalize messages, tools/results, errors, diff references and terminal turns; preserve source correlation and ledger ordering. Apply minimal retention/redaction rules before persistence.
acceptance: Supported native events map to stable domain events without duplicate effects on replay.
A timeline reconstructs after restart with native session/turn/item correlation and explicit gaps.
Tool output and transcript retention/redaction follow project settings; raw reasoning and secrets are excluded by default.
Terminal turns are captured independently of agent MCP reporting, including failed/interrupted statuses.
issues.verification: Replay sanitized duplicate/out-of-order/partial streams and verify persisted order, gap markers, redaction and terminal-event capture.

issues.title: Compile initial persona context and expose scoped AGCP MCP tools
issues.outcome: Give the root orchestrator deterministic task context and an authenticated narrow control surface.
issues.scope: Compile an initial versioned orchestrator context with objective, constraints, identity, authority references and reporting contract. Implement get_task_context, register_artifact, request_subagent and report_status with preliminary artifact records; richer registry protocols arrive in M5.
acceptance: The connector injects a deterministic context package and stores its digest/version references without logging secrets.
MCP derives task/project identity from the session capability and rejects forged parent/scope claims.
Tool inputs/outputs are schema-validated, and status reports cannot bypass legal transitions or accept their own completion.
Root session can retrieve context and publish a provenance-bearing artifact stub.
issues.verification: Exercise context determinism, foreign task IDs, revoked/expired capability calls, invalid schemas and a native session accessing the scoped MCP tools.

issues.title: Register policy-validated child sessions with isolated workspaces
issues.outcome: Allow controlled delegation while preserving registered identity, authority limits and source workspace safety.
issues.scope: Validate child role, parent, depth, budget, tool/data limits and workspace ownership before provisioning. Apply the worktree/checkout strategy from M0 and compensate partial session launch failures.
acceptance: An authorized root request creates a registered child task/session with correct parent and reduced scope.
Depth/budget/policy violations, forged parentage, authority expansion and unregistered spawn paths are rejected.
Concurrent writers receive isolated workspaces or explicit serialized ownership according to ADR 0002.
Partial provisioning and cancellation revoke credentials and release resources without orphaned active sessions.
issues.verification: Run root-to-child native flow plus denied depth/scope/budget cases, overlapping writer attempts and injected process-start failure.

issues.title: Implement immutable approval records and one-shot decision binding
issues.outcome: Create the exact-action boundary that every human or future agent decision must satisfy.
issues.scope: Normalize proven native approvals, freeze canonical action bytes/digest and original native correlation, and implement signed decision verification and durable single-use state transitions. Only supported exact-action kinds may enter the approval path.
acceptance: Approval identity binds project/task/session/turn/native request and immutable action content, allowed decision, expiry and policy snapshot.
Bridge validates the AGCP decision envelope before translating it to a supported one-action native response.
Wrong digest/session/resolver, invalid signature, expiry, unsupported decisions and reused requests cannot authorize execution.
Concurrent resolutions have one durable winner; missing immutable payload or uncertain state is unavailable/fail-closed rather than reconstructed from a model summary.
issues.verification: Use table-driven negative cases, concurrent resolution tests and canonicalization fixtures; verify a second request cannot reuse the first decision.

issues.title: Deliver human approval inbox and native accept/deny flow
issues.outcome: Let a human review and resolve a native pending action while Codex remains paused.
issues.scope: Surface pending approvals with what/why/target/impact/risk/expiry/evidence and current owner. Dispatch a verified one-shot response to the original pending request and reconcile native resolution outcomes. Use the accepted Operations desk direction with direct notification-card decisions and manual per-segment human group approval; see ADR 0003.
acceptance: A real native approval appears as pending and its original action remains paused until an explicit valid decision.
Approve and deny resolve only that original action, with durable human identity and policy/authority references.
Stale cards, double-clicks, disconnected sessions and insufficient capability cannot approve; UI distinguishes decision recorded from execution observed.
Session-wide permission and persistent policy amendments are unavailable in the initial one-action flow.
Notification cards expose Approve and Deny directly with action, agent, target, impact and risk visible; Inspect is optional for the decision.
Each approval segment has counted Approve all, with member exclusion changing it to Approve selected. The gesture freezes displayed member IDs/digests; new arrivals are excluded.

Every group member passes exact-action validation and receives its own audit/outcome. Expired, modified, disconnected or resolved members cannot be approved; partial outcomes are explicit and questions/blockers are excluded.
issues.verification: Demonstrate native approve/deny flows using harmless sentinel actions and exercise stale UI, duplicate submit and two simultaneous pending sessions. Verify inline decisions without inspector navigation, whole-group approval, member exclusion, new arrivals, mixed-validity members and independent outcomes; questions and context blockers remain unresolved.

issues.title: Harden approval expiry, disconnect, crash recovery and key loss
issues.outcome: Ensure a service failure cannot turn pending or uncertain approval delivery into unauthorized execution.
issues.scope: Implement expiry, cancellation, native request reconciliation, bounded retry, key storage/rotation or loss policy, and recovery of recorded versus dispatched decisions. Design for the crash window around native send.
acceptance: Service/connector disconnect, expired decision and unavailable verification keep actions denied or pending without accidental native acceptance.
Restart reconciles native pending requests; decisions are never replayed against a replacement action or newly reused native identifier.
A crash after send but before acknowledgement is marked uncertain and reconciled; there is no blind resend or unsupported exactly-once execution claim.
Missing/corrupted key material and interrupted audit writes have documented safe behavior and actionable operator recovery.
issues.verification: Inject failures before commit, after commit, around native send, during acknowledgement, on timeout and on key loss; assert no unreviewed sentinel side effect.

issues.title: Build approval-anchored Activity, Changes, Context and Decision Path inspector
issues.outcome: Give the human enough evidence to decide in AGCP without requiring a separate Codex UI.
issues.scope: Open the persisted session timeline anchored on the exact approval event. Keep the pending action visible while showing activity, supported diffs/change evidence, task/persona/artifact context, and human/policy decision ancestry.
acceptance: An approval card opens the correct session/event and remains pinned during navigation.
Activity shows preceding messages/tools/results with gaps explicit; Changes exposes available diff and Git references with unavailable evidence labeled.
Context shows task objective, parent, persona version, authority and workspace/sandbox summary; Decision Path shows recorded policy checks and resolver ancestry.
Resolution updates the same event view; future delegated judgments fit without fabricating them in the MVP.
issues.verification: Run a synthetic but persisted approval inspection flow and a live native session smoke check; verify wrong-session deep links, missing diff, long output and keyboard focus.

issues.title: Observe terminal turns and route advisory signals into parent inboxes
issues.outcome: Ensure a child question or blocker reaches the parent even when the child never calls a reporting tool.
issues.scope: Create TurnObservation records from connector events and advisory labels for awaiting_input, decision_proposal, blocker, completion_claim, progress_update and ambiguous. Route source-linked inbox messages idempotently.
acceptance: Every meaningful terminal/waiting child turn creates a source-linked observation and a parent inbox entry without an MCP call.
Questions, decisions and blockers alert the parent; interrupted/failed turns retain true terminal status.
Classifier failure/uncertainty retains an ambiguous observation; labels cannot approve actions, terminate sessions or accept task completion.
Repeated native events produce no duplicate notifications or review turns; root/orphan handling is defined.
issues.verification: Replay question, blocker, progress, completion, ambiguous, failed and interrupted fixture turns, including duplicates and classifier outage; demonstrate one native child question flow.

issues.title: Add parent/human inbox replies and bounded review-turn scheduling
issues.outcome: Close the conversational loop while keeping human approval authority and session ownership explicit.
issues.scope: Add reply, request revision, propose/accept completion and escalate operations with identity checks. Schedule bounded parent review turns through the registered connector and guard against recursive wakeups and overlapping turns.
acceptance: Parent or human replies reach the exact registered child session and retain message provenance.
Parent review is bounded by budget/deadline; unavailable parents surface an escalation instead of blocking indefinitely.
Completion acceptance follows task policy and remains separate from an advisory completion claim.
Inbox messages and model output cannot bypass the native approval inbox; duplicate routing and review loops are bounded.
issues.verification: Demonstrate child question → parent inbox → parent/human reply → child continuation; test foreign-parent calls, busy parent, timeout and repeated notification loops.

issues.title: Version persona and skill templates and ship the MVP role library
issues.outcome: Make session behavior reproducible as personas and attached procedures evolve.
issues.scope: Implement immutable persona/skill versions, clone/edit UI and session version pinning. Provide orchestrator, architect, senior/junior implementer, codebase analyst, security reviewer, test engineer, release reviewer and research personas.
acceptance: All nine PRD roles declare mandate, authority template, tool/data scope, escalation, required inputs, expected outputs and completion contract.
Editing/cloning creates a new immutable version; existing sessions keep their original versions and context digest.
Skills declare procedures and input/output/capability requirements and can attach to multiple personas.
Persona editing cannot self-grant authority or expand a running session capability.
issues.verification: Compile representative personas, compare version/digest stability, and exercise attempted scope expansion and missing required metadata.
issues.references: PRD §8 personas and skills; technical spec §§3–4.

issues.title: Implement versioned logical artifact registry and permitted resolution
issues.outcome: Let agents resolve project inputs by logical key with trustworthy version, provenance and freshness.
issues.scope: Extend initial artifact records into versioned content/external references, approval/status, provenance, access scope, and freshness. Support current_roadmap and codebase_map logical keys.
acceptance: Resolution returns only an approved, readable, non-stale version for the caller/project.
External GitHub files/issues/PRs/commits and AGCP-native content are supported without duplicating private content into Git.
Supersession, revoked access, missing artifacts and source-commit freshness produce explicit results.
Task UI and inspector show linked artifact version and provenance.
issues.verification: Exercise stale/current branches, superseded versions, denied scope, missing inputs and external-reference records using synthetic examples.

issues.title: Enforce required artifact context protocols before issue planning
issues.outcome: Prevent agents from proceeding with missing, stale or unauthorized planning context.
issues.scope: Implement protocol precondition checks at session compilation and governed side-effect execution. Provide an issue-planning flow requiring approved current_roadmap and a sufficiently fresh codebase_map.
acceptance: Missing/stale/unapproved/unreadable required artifacts block the operation or create an explicit escalation.
Successful compilation pins artifact versions, source commit and freshness evidence in provenance.
Re-check requirements immediately before an external write so context changes cannot bypass validation.
A successful demo resolves logical keys, publishes issue proposals and preserves source input references.
issues.verification: Run missing/stale/foreign input cases plus a valid planning flow; change an input between proposal and write and confirm revalidation blocks or requires a fresh proposal.

issues.title: Add optional GitHub authorization, repository linking and read-only references
issues.outcome: Connect engineering artifacts without making GitHub credentials a prerequisite for local governance.
issues.scope: Implement the M0-selected authorization approach, capability/status UI, repository linking and read-only issue/PR/commit/file reference resolution. Store secret references via secure storage, not the database.
acceptance: The full local project/session/approval workflow works with GitHub unconfigured.
Authorization scopes distinguish read, write, administration and release capability; UI does not imply unavailable permissions.
A project links a repository and resolves permitted engineering references with provenance.
Revocation, wrong account/repository and rate-limit failures are recoverable without leaking credentials.
issues.verification: Use sanitized HTTP fixtures for scope, revocation and rate-limit behavior plus a least-privilege read-only smoke check against an owned test repository.
issues.references: PRD §§7.1, 8 GitHub integration; technical spec §§1, 11; ADR 0002.

issues.title: Govern GitHub repository and issue creation with exact proposals
issues.outcome: Allow explicit engineering side effects while preserving approval and context provenance.
issues.scope: Implement application-owned proposals for repository creation and issue creation. Bind account/owner/repository/visibility or issue title/body/labels to immutable approval data. Keep merge, collaborator, permissions and release operations unavailable for the MVP.
acceptance: A human-approved repository proposal creates exactly the chosen owner/name/visibility, then links it to the project.
Issue creation requires current artifact inputs, scoped GitHub authorization and a valid exact-proposal human decision.
Changed title/body/target/visibility or invalid context invalidates the old decision; denied proposals cause no write.
Network failure/retry reconciles existing external results before retrying, avoiding duplicate repos/issues; resulting references and decisions are audited.
issues.verification: Exercise approved/denied/stale/modified proposals, insufficient scope and ambiguous network completion with fixtures. Run controlled writes in an explicitly designated owned test target for live acceptance.

issues.title: Verify all MVP journeys and security/recovery release gates
issues.outcome: Provide concrete evidence for all eight PRD acceptance criteria before calling the project an MVP.
issues.scope: Create a repeatable acceptance matrix with synthetic projects and a supported native Codex version. Include cross-project identity, token revocation, decision replay/expiry, local boundary, redaction, recovery and optional GitHub failure cases.
acceptance: All eight PRD acceptance criteria have reproducible steps, expected outcomes and evidence links.
At least the session, child, native approval and conversational routing journeys run against a real supported connector, not fixtures alone.
Negative security/recovery scenarios fail closed, with no unresolved release-blocking defect.
Document measured approval pause/resume reliability and capability limits; avoid unproven encryption or audit-integrity claims.
issues.verification: Run the full acceptance matrix from a clean local state and retain only sanitized summaries and synthetic fixtures in the repository. Open linked defects for any failures and keep the milestone open.
issues.references: PRD §§9–11; technical spec §§6–12; docs/ROADMAP.md acceptance matrix.

issues.title: Package the local MVP and document onboarding, recovery and limits
issues.outcome: Make the verified single-user local application installable and understandable.
issues.scope: Package for the initial target OS and document prerequisites, Codex version/auth, startup/shutdown, data location, security model, recovery, optional GitHub authorization and supported capabilities. Resolve licensing before distributing.
acceptance: A clean-machine or clean-account walkthrough installs and runs the verified project/session/approval flow.
Operator docs explain pending/denied/uncertain decisions, key loss and backup/recovery using actual behavior.
Release notes identify unsupported native UI/coexistence or approval categories and the supported version matrix.
Distribution license is explicit; artifacts exclude credentials, local project content and session data; release checklist records checks and known limits.
issues.verification: Perform the documented onboarding and recovery walkthrough against the packaged build; inspect distribution contents and verify application/CI checks remain green.
issues.references: PRD §§1, 5, 11–12; technical spec §§11–12; AGCP-003 licensing decision.

issues.title: Add bounded parent authority, delegated decisions and escalation
issues.outcome: Allow eligible parents to resolve child approvals without weakening the exact-action or human-only boundary.
issues.scope: Implement authority grants and policy predicates, nearest eligible parent routing, bounded approval review turns and escalation. Treat clarify/narrow/split as workflow outcomes requiring fresh action identity when content changes.
acceptance: A parent resolves only capabilities/targets/decision types within an unexpired grant and delegation depth.
Human-only categories, missing evidence and unauthorized/failed/timed-out parents escalate to the next eligible resolver.
Agents cannot change parentage, self-grant authority, expand tool scope or approve modified action content.
Decision Path shows every judgment, authority/policy version, escalation reason and exact bound decision.
issues.verification: Run a multi-level authority matrix with human-only categories, expired grants, timeout, forged ancestry and replacement actions; verify the original child remains paused until a valid resolution.

issues.title: Add transparent recommendation bundles over immutable approval nodes
issues.outcome: Reduce repetitive human review without hiding the atomic actions being authorized.
issues.scope: Build on the MVP manual human grouping from AGCP-014 / ADR 0003. Create recommendation-only bundles, member inspection/removal and member-specific resolution. Keep each approval node, digest, expiry and outcome permanent and independently auditable.
acceptance: A bundle never replaces or merges atomic approval identity or authority checks.
A human can inspect/remove individual members before deciding.
Expired/changed/unavailable members cannot inherit a bundle decision; partial outcomes are explicit.
Audit and inspector retain member provenance, recommendation author and individual native dispatch outcomes.
issues.verification: Test mixed validity, member removal, changed action, concurrent member resolution and partial dispatch failure.
issues.references: PRD §8 approval governance, 12 Next; technical spec §7.

issues.title: Implement redacted project export/import and integrity validation
issues.outcome: Allow portable governance metadata without exporting credentials or private source by default.
issues.scope: Define a versioned archive with redaction options, references, integrity metadata and safe import. Rebind external identities explicitly; never revive imported approvals or capabilities.
acceptance: Default export excludes source code, credentials, capability/signing material and raw session content.
Import validates archive schema/integrity and prevents path traversal, resource exhaustion and cross-project identity collision.
Imported history remains historical; pending decisions, sessions and grants are inactive until explicitly re-established.
Round-trip metadata and external references preserve provenance with redaction and integrity limits documented.
issues.verification: Round-trip synthetic projects; inspect default archive contents and reject tampered, malicious-path, oversize and incompatible-version archives.
